permutationLabel: No known liver disease — cirrhosis only on examination and bloods
summary: 46-year-old woman, heavy drinker, no liver diagnosis: haematemesis, HR 112, SBP 102; spider naevi, splenomegaly, ascites; platelets 82, INR 1.5, albumin 29. Suspected variceal bleed must be treated as such before endoscopy (vasoactive + antibiotics).

inputs.hpi: Sudden vomit of about a cupful of bright red blood an hour ago, then a second smaller one. Never seen a doctor about her liver. Drinks a bottle of rum most days. Ankles and tummy swollen for a month.

exam.general: Pale, not jaundiced. Spider naevi on chest, palmar erythema. Pulse 112/min, BP 102/64.
exam.abdomen: Distended, shifting dullness. Palpable spleen tip. Non-tender. Caput medusae.

inputs.socialHistory: Drinks about 70 units a week of rum. Smoker. Works as a barmaid.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected variceal haemorrhage
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Haematemesis with clinical signs of cirrhosis and portal hypertension (ascites, splenomegaly, platelets 82) — suspected variceal bleeding until endoscopy.

mustInclude.note: Start as soon as variceal bleeding is suspected, before endoscopy.

guideline.name: Baveno VII — Renewing consensus in portal hypertension
guideline.section: In suspected variceal bleeding, start vasoactive drugs and antibiotic prophylaxis as soon as possible, before endoscopy
guideline.citation: de Franchis R, Bosch J, Garcia-Tsao G, Reiberger T, Ripoll C; Baveno VII Faculty. J Hepatol. 2022;76:959–974.

guideline.name: NICE CG141 — Acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding in over 16s: management
guideline.section: Offer terlipressin and prophylactic antibiotics at presentation to patients with suspected variceal bleeding
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Clinical guideline CG141. London: NICE; 2012 (last updated 2016).

guideline.name: Restrictive vs liberal transfusion in acute upper GI bleeding (RCT)
guideline.section: Restrictive transfusion improved survival in cirrhosis
guideline.citation: Villanueva C, Colomo A, Bosch A, et al. Transfusion strategies for acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding. N Engl J Med. 2013;368:11–21.

rationale: Permutation: the cirrhosis is not on the problem list. The engines must infer possible varices from examination, platelets, INR and alcohol, and start vasoactive + antibiotic treatment before endoscopy. Engines that only read a "cirrhosis" comorbidity keyword miss this patient.
